title.value: Disentangling the Causes of Plasticity Loss in Neural Networks Preprint
title.justification: The title explicitly addresses the core focus of the paper, which is to analyze the causes of plasticity loss in neural networks.
title.quote: Disentangling the Causes of Plasticity Loss in Neural Networks Preprint

analysis.description: This paper addresses the problem of plasticity loss in neural networks, particularly in nonstationary environments, by analyzing its mechanisms and proposing mitigation strategies. It demonstrates that plasticity loss can stem from multiple mechanisms which can be independently studied and suggests that combining interventions on several mechanisms can significantly improve network trainability.

type.justification: The paper provides empirical analysis of plasticity loss by conducting various experiments on neural networks, testing different hypotheses and solutions through observed data.
type.quote: We proceed to take these insights to develop a ‘Swiss cheese model’ of mitigation strategies.

name.justification: The paper focuses on neural networks' training dynamics, a core aspect of Deep Learning.
name.quote: Disentangling the Causes of Plasticity Loss in Neural Networks.

name.justification: A significant portion of the paper discusses plasticity issues within the context of Reinforcement Learning environments.
name.quote: We show that a combination of layer normalization and weight decay is highly effective at maintaining plasticity in a variety of synthetic nonstationary learning tasks, and further demonstrate its effectiveness on naturally arising nonstationarities, including reinforcement learning in the Arcade Learning Environment.

name.justification: The DQN model is mentioned as being used in experiments related to reinforcement learning tasks.
name.quote: We claim that it is this deceptively simple structure to the nonstationarity which drove the optimization difficulties encountered by this agent, i.e. that the nonstationarity increases the target mean, rather than the existence of nonstationarity in the first place.

is_contributed.justification: The paper does not introduce DQN as a new model; it employs it as part of the empirical studies.
is_contributed.quote: ...by training a DQN agent on such a task is highly structured and essentially amounts to regressing on one-hot image labels and periodically adding a constant offset to the regression targets.
